title: H3936 (124th General Assembly): Firearms - Bump Stock Unlawful

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2021-02-23; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess124_2021-2022/prever/3936_20210223.htm (LegiScan doc 2306548))

operative_text:
Section 1 (new Section 16-23-540(A)): It is unlawful for a person to possess, distribute, or manufacture a part, component, attachment, device, or accessory designed to accelerate the rate of fire of a semiautomatic weapon including, but not limited to, a bump stock or trigger crank.
Section 1 (new Section 16-23-540(B)): A person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction, must be imprisoned not more than five years.
Section 2: Within ninety days of the effective date of this act, persons possessing, distributing, or manufacturing a part, component, attachment, device, or accessory designed to accelerate the rate of fire of a semiautomatic weapon must cease all operations concerning the distribution or manufacture of these items and surrender such items to their local sheriff's department, the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division, or a field office of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives.
